html:
Who He Is

General Alexis, nicknamed the Silver Fox, was one of the two generals of the Crown who commanded half of the Imperial Army at the time of the 1774 Summer Games. According to the courtiers, he constantly arranged constructions, exercises and maneuvers, read all the books about military affairs and considered himself the best commander of the empire, although he did not command the army in any real war. Until 1774, he was not married and in the eyes of some girls remained “a piece of cake ... although a little dried up.” The general belongs to the genus Foremother Sophia - Mira was surprised to learn that he was so high-born - and owns Smile Island in the East Sea, which gives an advantage to the merchant fleet of the Crown in competition with the Southern Way.

Biography

In "Arrow, Coin, Spark"

At the 1774 Summer Ball, Alexis danced with Mira; she felt he was a skilled dancer, but lacked mischief and freedom. He was the only one who listened seriously to Valerie Gracend’s song about love for Adrian: half-covering his eyes, frowning dreamily, and became the subject of ridicule. (Valerie Graysend) At the open reception of the Emperor of Peace, introducing herself to him, a dispute arose about the construction of the army: she doubted whether it was reasonable to put a spark infantry in the center, which, having spent its charges, would become defenseless. The general, who at first was bored, became carried away, proved that sparkers would wipe out any enemy before the charges ran out, and caught himself, only realizing that he was leading a military council with a seventeen-year-old girl.

He came to the reception for the request of the Third Marine Guild of the Southern Way, patronized by the Gracelands and the Duke of Labelin: the sailors asked to arrange a parking on Smile Island. The baron replied to the guild that he would do as the emperor pleased, and "did not mind" providing his coves. Adrian saw this as a Graysend manipulation and refused. Mira realized that the general wanted to do Valerie a favor and that he was in love with her. Later, writing a version of the conspiracy, Mira suspected that Valerie could use the feelings of a general whose regiment stood in Faunterra during the summer games, although Alexis herself was considered "simple and reliable." The “last argument” against Labelin for her was precisely the Duke’s new friendship with the general, which Mark pointed out to her. In the Place de la Concorde, she saw the fox on a white horse, in full ceremonial armor, despite the heat, taking command of the arriving regiment of Theodore the Great; from a distance his ragged face was imperceptible, and in armor he seemed handsome.

In "Only One Star"

When Adrian called Minerva the bride, Alexis asked Valerie's hand, and the Graysends considered "the best general of the Crown, the owner of strategically important islands" a worthy consolation prize. The mutiny of the northerners benefited him "even twice": the general married and became the commander-in-chief of all the troops of the Crown, and his rival William Davey, the commander of the South Wing, was in disfavor. (William Davy) In a training match at the military council, Adrian attacked, and the general steamed until the emperor disarmed him.

Together with Valerie Alexis, he asked the lord for permission to immediately march against Origin by the forces of seven regiments of the northern corps, promising to crush the rebel “in one month”. Adrian, exposing Valerie, reproached the general that he was driven by the anxiety of his wife for the possession of the Greysends. Alexis studied Desmond Origin's Questions of the Commander and believed that Erwin was fighting "according to the textbook" because he could not do otherwise, and that he would not fall into a trap on the hills. It was on this council that the joker Manson shouted "There and back!", prompting Adrian to plan what he called a "wedding present" to the general.

At the beginning of the Northern War, Alexis commanded spark regiments in the south of the Empire, while Adrian himself demonstratively left for Litland. The Emperor secretly transferred seven regiments that landed in the Southern Way and joined Alexis, and on December 2, 1774, Alexis defeated the Northerners at the Battle of Pixie. He sheltered the army in the woods, putting only small detachments under the flags of the Southern Way on the edge, approached the Origin camp by night march, moved spark regiments to the center, and threw a heavy cavalry into the gap between Northwood and Statham; Craig Northwood, who broke through to his headquarters, met two reserve spark regiments and surrounded him. Then he skillfully organized the persecution, declared a thousand Hilt for the head of the fleeing Erwin Origin and briefly reported to the lord: “By the will of the gods, we won! .. The Northwood brothers are in captivity. Tomorrow we will enter the Labelin."

However, when he entered the Labelin and quartered the shelves throughout the city, he fell into a trap (the Labelin massacre): five battalions of kire, sitting in the catacombs, killed the sentries at night, captured the streets and cut the sleeping. (Labelin; Night in Labelin) Eight and a half thousand soldiers of Alexis were captured; of an army of fifty thousand shields and twelve thousand spark copies, he was able to withdraw the incomplete four regiments in an organized manner. He took the prisoner Craig Northwood with him, and in retreat, he destroyed the bridges over Hanai and the railroads, winning three weeks for Adrian. He brought the remains of the regiments to Faunterra, but the palace occupied by Origin did not storm. When Mira, already a widow, came to the capital, the general, "as if he had lived ten years," reported the situation to her; leaving to negotiate with the rebel, she told him to launch an assault if he did not return in an hour.

"A Doll on the Throne"

Oath

In the third week after the coronation, Alexis, whom the Lord Chancellor's secretariat had refused to allow to the Lady, obtained a meeting through Colonel-General Statham and insisted that Minerva personally take the oath of the remainder of his army - incomplete three regiments out of fifteen, and in fact five battalions. (Minerva's Coronation) Mira refused at first, but she was ashamed and went. The soldiers, according to the general, remembered that she alone went to negotiations with the rebel and thereby saved most of them from death. Mira took an oath from each company separately to "see all faces", and the general, against any protocol, thanked her. At the same time, he angrily said that Origin appointed his rival, General Gore, the supreme commander-in-chief of the Crown Lands. Erwin himself soon admitted that Horus' corps was at his disposal, but Silver Fox's corps was "absolutely devoted to the sovereign", and could only be subdued through Minerva.

The Lord's Resistance

The soldiers of Lis became the support of Minerva: they guarded the arrested ministers, took the relatives of Dreyfus Born into custody. The general openly hated Origin for the night Labelin: according to him, he, broken "on an honest battlefield", hit secretly, and his people even dressed as bandits, changing clothes with the Labelin swaddle. The general had enough funds to maintain only three regiments, and he refused to allocate people from them for the needs of the treasury. In March 1775, on the day of the opening of navigation, Alexis was next to Minerva on the schooner "Striking", where she, holding the family of Minister Dreyfus Bourne hostage, forced him to confess to embezzlement; looking after the Minister, the general with disgusted anger remarked: "The serp is punished ... (Dreyfus Born) But the damn spark lives and lives!” When news came of Moran's attack on Melorange, Alexis warned that Origin's campaign would make him "the ruler of the South and the West", and suggested a maneuver: two regiments moved along the rails to strike not south, but west, to Holliwell. In negotiations with Moran, Minerva showed Shavan pigeons with an order to Silver Fox "not to occupy the Cool Throat"; a bluff based on this maneuver forced the horde to leave. Later, through the staff of General Alexis, where the officer on duty received his letter, Agent Moger Buckley of the Labelins obtained an audience with Minerva. Erwin in his notebook drew on the general a caricature - a rail tractor, "decisive, bold, assertive", which can not get off the rails.

Disclosure

At a secret meeting of her supporters, Peace listed Lisa's merits - "a brilliant maneuver, by the forces of a single regiment, driven a whole horde into a dead end" - and then accused him of being ordered to make her a real ruler. She checked this with Statham: in seeking a meeting, the general named her the purpose of taking the oath in advance. Robert Origin's kairas surrounded Fox. When asked about Adrian's death, the general swore to Sophia that he was not involved; when asked if he had lost the night-time Labelin intentionally, he put a spark dagger to his heart:

“I fought with a rebel. At the limit. I did what I could. He cheated. Me."

Mira believed it, and the general asked to speak in private, vowing that he was on her side "whatever happens."

"The Hunt" and "Those We Forgive"

Mira revealed to Erwin the secret of the Fox: after the death of Telurian, the general became the eyes, ears and hand of the Lady-in-the-Dark in Faunterra and with her help looked after Adrian, and her order was to prevent Agatha from the throne at any cost. (Lady in the Dark) According to Myra, Lis and his mistress help her while she defends Yangmei's interests; if she marries Origin or cedes the throne to him, she will be rid of her, and the next heiress is Lady in Darkness herself. Those We Forgive describes "the day of the exposure of General Alexis Smile" through the eyes of Captain Chatterhand: the general assured that he would never go against the mistress and that the goals of his second mistress were "bright and noble"; Minerva, referring to the play about the servant of two masters, decided to leave him life and rank, “because he is useful”, not knowing whether he can forgive. Erwin, assessing the strength of her rival in May 1775, believed that she had only "beaten three regiments of Alexis", which she can no longer trust, and later said that the Silver Fox taught a lesson: the officers of the guard also need supervision.

In "Humans and Gods"

Mira believed that a general loyal to Lady in Darkness needed a replacement, and called him a man of "triple loyalty": he served her, a secret order and would be happy to serve Adrian if he was resurrected. Any northern lord she thought would have thrown him into prison a long time ago. Lady Sophia Origin, handing out masks to General Davey, sarcastically described Smile as a man who "for a gull of Minerva, but also for a frog from the swamps." In early June, Minerva invited the general with the pregnant Valerie to the Small Tea Room to find out whose side he would choose if Adrian appeared; Valerie spent the entire meal talking about the future child, the general gently patted her on the back and anxiously looked at the mistress, and Mira thought of making Valerie a second frailty - "at the same time both honor and threat" - but never began a difficult conversation. The fox himself grumbled that the quiet "Snowdrops" only accumulate strength before the storm.

The Shadow of the Great Tree

Before the horde of Paul

When the horde with the Rings invaded Almera, Alexis at the military council mercilessly explained to the mistress the arrangement: eighteen thousand horsemen with three dozen Rings make up fifteen cavalry battalions, each of which is able to dispel the spark regiment; The fingers beat further than the long bows, and all tactics against the light cavalry collapse. His longtime rival Gore agreed with him this time. Later, Lis presented an idea that Mira considered truly brilliant: The Rings beat in a straight line, and the bows and catapults are a canopy, which means that a simple earthshaft will protect from the Rings. During the exercises, he was pleased to see by the chronometer that the regiment takes combat order in sixteen minutes.

Treason

As the horde moved to the Crownlands, the Silver Fox's hull was moved west, to the banks of the Back. In the summer of 1775, a general with three regiments stood at the edge of the river Back, but the Shavans of Johan Reis bypassed him and the kire, crossing downstream. (Beck) Having received the order together with Northern General Horton to stop the horde on the Snake, he did not fulfill it, threw positions and went to the Crownlands, keeping complete silence; Mira found out about his betrayal from Horton. Back in July, at the table of Baron Darryl in Labelin, Adrian's allies hoped that Valerie, who owed Maurice Labelin and was friendly with Magda, would receive a secret message, "turn the Silver Fox swords in the right direction." (Hugo Derrill) According to Magda, he was persuaded by Valerie to side with Adrian, having received one letter from the Labelins; Valerie was carrying a child at the time, and Magda made her her her first frailty. When Adrian entered Faunterra, Lis reported to the lord that the city was under complete control, and the Parliamentarians came to Minerva familiar to her officers of his corps. The same regiments she had sworn were deployed under the walls, and Mira expected that Fox, beaten in the night Labelin, would advise Adrian to enter the city in the dark. General William Davey, sent to Main, later bitterly told Minerva that "Smile and Gore changed their oath", and a dual power was established in Faunterra.

At the court of Adrian

In the autumn, the general, together with Horus, followed Adrian to the North. In December, in Main, Alexis, at the request of Adrian, commented for the court on the battle of the First Winter, which was shown by the Bird without the Cloth, pointing the sword at the ice fortifications and predicting a heavy beginning for Shayland; he explained to the court that Minerva had used the Glove of Power as a throwing weapon, with a sword-pointer pars the success of the Almer regiment. (Battle for First Winter; Bird without Flesh; Glove of Might) When events did not go according to the forecast and the sunsets fled from the city in panic, he fell silent with the lord. In peace talks with the Origins, when Robert Origin twisted Lady-in-the-Dark's neck in revenge for his father, the Silver Fox snatched the sword with the cry of "Treason! Murder!" and yelled that the Origins had broken the word about safety. Even at the table, Iona felt a “hidden hatred” in him. Robert replied that the guarantees concerned only Adrian and his men. After the murder, Lis stayed in the hall with Hyder Leed and Jemis when Erwin sent out a guard and Adrian had a crucial conversation.

In "Fantasies"

The author calls the stories “Fantasies” possible destinies of heroes. The action of "Deadly Evidence" takes place in June 1777 in Winslow, in the Southern Way. Lady Valerie Gracend-Smile gave birth there to twins, two strong men of six pounds. Her husband, a retired general, was invited to teach a military history course at the University of Faunterra. To go with him to the capital, Valerie refused: the capital excitement, according to her, will give the milk a gallbladder taste. According to Valerie, “my Alexis” and Count Quindar became friends “on the basis of confrontation with wolves.” The local priest Farnsworth, being in danger, wanted to ask General Smile for help. Valerie replied that the general in Faunterra had no previous influence: "he is no longer a general, but a teacher." Farnsworth was murdered at the gate of her estate. The lawyer Mac, by all indications - Mark retired, deduced that a secret monastic organization was behind the murder. He named her the Silver Fox and the Second of the Five. It was run by the late Lady in the Dark, and the general himself, according to him, "was convicted of working for the order."

In the full edition of the collection, Valerie explains the resignation of her husband to the revenge of the northerners: the Lord Chancellor allegedly long ago hated “my Alexis” for his victory over the kairs at Pixie and achieved his dismissal under the guise of reforming the spark army. Mack, on the other hand, says that Lis “turned Minerva right and left for the sake of order affairs” and was expelled from the service immediately after the election; Minerva allegedly wanted to take away his estate and title, but for him stood up for the seigneur - Labelin, "Dolphin defended Fox", and the general saved the barony "and some influence."

Personality and Appearance

A representative, powerful physique lord with gray sideburns and a beard; the face is dug with ospins ("beards are sick"), which makes it even uglier when excited. The voice is powerful and low. Serious to the gloom, straightforward, pedantic in military affairs and faithful to the protocol, but capable of strong feelings - love for Valerie and hatred for Origin. Manson disliked him for his excessive seriousness, although he considered him a good soldier. Mira noticed that the annoyance and anger come from his ugly face when he is completely focused on the military task.

Trivia

  • Responding to Adrian at the council, Alexis pondered, drawing an eight-in-the-air training sword.
  • Smile and Gore fought for many years for the post of commander-in-chief: both received it, both lost and both gloated at each other.
  • In the summer of 1774, a jealous Valerie abandoned Myra, who was then known as Gloria Northwood, that she was loved by "everyone: the horse, his lordship, the fox Alexis, even the jester."
  • Hampton Bridge was reportedly set on fire by General Alexis' retreating troops.

Appearances

  • "Arrow, coin, spark" - the first appearance (ball, open reception, parade).
  • "Only one star" - the advice of Adrian, Pixy, Labelin, a meeting with Minerva in the capital.
  • "A Doll on the Throne" - the oath of the regiments, exposure.
  • "The Yanmei Hunt", "Those We Forgive", "Humans and Gods" - the secret of the general and its consequences.
  • "The Shadow of the Great Tree" - Minerva's advice, betrayal, Adrian's court.
  • "Fantasies" - "Deathly Evidence"; mentioned in "Ad-ri-an!" (General Smile's troops have not yet arrived at Faunterra)
